hooks.text: The first confirmed black hole shoots jets at half light speed.
A stellar heavyweight 7,000 light-years away is actively tearing apart its companion.
Twin plasma jets from a black hole shine with 10,000 suns.

title: The First Black Hole Ever Found Is Shooting Dancing Jets
description: Discover how Cygnus X-1, the first confirmed black hole, strips its companion star and fires superheated plasma jets across space.

beats.text: The first confirmed black hole shoots jets at half light speed.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of Cygnus X-1 binary system, NASA illustration, 2011

beats.text: Discovered in 1964 during a sounding rocket flight, Cygnus X-1 sits roughly 7,000 light-years away.
beats.visual: Aerobee sounding rocket launch, White Sands missile range, historical photo

beats.text: The system features a black hole with a mass of about 21 suns orbiting a star named HDE 226868.
beats.visual: Cygnus constellation map, astrophotography Milky Way region

beats.text: Both objects complete a tight orbit every 5.6 days at a distance of just one-fifth the Earth-Sun gap.
beats.visual: Black hole accretion disk diagram, NASA illustration
queries: Black hole accretion disk diagram NASA

beats.text: As material streams inward, it forms a superheated accretion disk that blazes brightly in X-rays.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray Observatory spacecraft illustration in orbit, NASA photo

beats.text: Yet the most mind-bending record is its twin plasma jets racing outward at immense speeds.
beats.visual: Black hole relativistic jets illustration, ESO concept art
queries: Active galactic nucleus jet ESO concept

beats.text: These blazing jets shine with the energy of 10,000 suns while visibly swaying like dancing beams.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope high resolution photo in Earth orbit, NASA
queries: Hubble Space Telescope high resolution photo
